```{r setup-pca, include=FALSE}
library(here)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 7, dpi = 110)
source(here("analysis", "reports", "descriptive_plots", "R", "PCA.R"))    # pca_block(), BLOCKS, thresholds
```

```{=html}
<h1 id="per-block-pca">Per-block PCA: does each block have a structure?</h1>

<div class="block-box">
<strong>The screen above and this section decompose the same matrix.</strong>
A correlation screen answers &ldquo;which <em>pairs</em> of items are
near-duplicates?&rdquo;. It cannot answer &ldquo;does this block have a
<em>structure</em>?&rdquo; &mdash; a block can contain no pair above
|<em>r</em>|&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.5 and still be two clean dimensions, or be one
dimension with a tail of weakly related items. What follows runs a principal
component analysis on exactly the same Spearman matrix each figure above plots,
so the two read as one argument rather than two analyses.
<br><br>
<strong>These components are estimated within one block at a time.</strong>
The pooled sub-scale solution of the pilot reports ran one analysis over the
belief and behaviour items together. C1 here is not the C1
there, and the two numberings must never be read as interchangeable. This is a
check on whether the blocks are sensible groupings, not a replacement for that
solution.
<br><br>
<strong>Two blocks are deliberately not the same columns as the screen.</strong>
Beliefs and Behaviour use the reverse-scored copies, so that high means
&ldquo;more pro-liberalisation&rdquo; on every item; without that the sign of a
loading would record how an item happened to be worded rather than what
respondents think, and the first component would come out as a wording artefact
instead of a dimension.
<br><br>
<strong>How many components each block gets</strong> is decided by parallel
analysis (Horn, 1965) rather than by eigenvalues over 1, which is known to
over-extract. Blocks shorter than five items are not asked the question at all:
with three or four items there is not enough covariance structure for a second
component to mean anything, and rotation is undefined for a single one.
</div>
```

```{r pca-retention, echo=TRUE}
# PCA.R is sourced in the setup chunk; its RUN_STANDALONE guard means nothing
# ran on import. pca_block() is the same function `Rscript PCA.R` calls, so the
# console script and this tab cannot drift apart.
# BLOCKS_FITTED rather than BLOCKS: a block with fewer than two items has no
# component solution, and in the pooled dataset `Behaviour` has none at all.
pca_results <- lapply(names(BLOCKS_FITTED),
                      function(b) pca_block(BLOCKS_FITTED[[b]], b, pilot))
names(pca_results) <- names(BLOCKS_FITTED)

knitr::kable(
  do.call(rbind, lapply(pca_results, `[[`, "retention")),
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = paste("How many components each block supports. 'Parallel' is what",
                  "parallel analysis suggests, 'Kaiser' counts eigenvalues",
                  "over 1 (shown for comparison only - it over-extracts), and",
                  "'Retained' is what was actually fitted."))
```

**Read `n/item` first.** It is the thinnest part of this soft launch: a stable
component solution wants something like 10 respondents per item, and the
`n/item` column shows how far each block is from that. Nothing below is a result about drug
attitudes — it is a check on whether the blocks hang together well enough to be
worth keeping as blocks.

```{r pca-blocks, echo=TRUE, results='asis', fig.height=6.2, fig.width=9.5}
# One section per block: the diagnostics that decide whether the solution is
# readable at all, then the loadings, then the two figures. `results='asis'`
# so the per-block headings become real headings in the sidebar.
for (result in pca_results) {
  k     <- result$retention$Retained
  items <- nrow(result$table)

  cat("\n\n## ", result$block, " (", items, " items, ", k, " component",
      if (k != 1) "s", ")\n\n", sep = "")

  # The caveats that decide how much weight the solution can carry, stated
  # rather than implied.
  notes <- c(
    if (result$thin)
      paste0("**Reduced report.** Fewer than ", MIN_ITEMS_PCA, " items: one ",
             "component, no rotation, no per-component reliability. A block ",
             "this short cannot support a component structure, and its KMO is ",
             "near meaningless."),
    if (result$n_obs / items < 10)
      paste0("**", round(result$n_obs / items, 1), " respondents per item.** ",
             "Treat the solution as provisional."),
    if (result$n_obs < nrow(pilot))
      paste0("The correlation matrix is pairwise over all ", nrow(pilot),
             " respondents; parallel analysis and reliability use the ",
             result$n_obs, " complete cases."),
    if (any(result$near_constant))
      paste0("**Near-constant items:** ",
             paste0("`", result$table$variable[result$near_constant], "` (",
                    round(100 * result$modal_share[result$near_constant]),
                    "% give one answer)", collapse = ", "),
             ". Too little variance to load anywhere; consider dropping them ",
             "before reading the solution."),
    paste0("KMO = ", round(result$kmo$MSA, 2), " (lowest item ",
           names(which.min(result$kmo$MSAi)), " = ",
           round(min(result$kmo$MSAi), 2), ")",
           if (result$kmo$MSA < 0.50) ", below 0.50 and barely factorable",
           "; Bartlett *p* ",
           format.pval(result$bartlett$p.value, eps = .001),
           "; ", round(sum(result$var_pc[seq_len(k)]), 1),
           "% of variance in ", k, " component", if (k != 1) "s",
           " (", result$rotation, " rotation)."),
    if (!result$thin)
      paste0("Reliability: ",
             paste0("C", seq_len(k), " ", result$n_members, " items, ",
                    ifelse(is.na(result$alphas), "too few for alpha",
                           paste0("alpha = ", round(result$alphas, 2))),
                    collapse = "; "), ".")
  )
  cat(paste(notes, collapse = "\n\n"), "\n\n")

  loading_table <- result$table[order(result$table$primary,
                                      -result$table$prim_load), ]
  # left at full length: a kable cell wraps in HTML, so truncating here only
  # loses the end of items that share an opening clause
  print(knitr::kable(
    loading_table[, setdiff(names(loading_table), c("block", "prim_load"))],
    row.names = FALSE,
    caption = paste0(result$block, ": loadings, sorted by component. ",
                     "'primary' is the component an item belongs to, or - if ",
                     "its strongest loading is under ", LOAD_MIN, ".")))
  cat("\n\n")

  print(result$scree)
  print(result$loadings_plot)
}
```
